title: ChatGPT Based Data Augmentation for Improved Parameter-Efficient Debiasing of LLMs
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured social bias against religious groups by quantifying a model's preference for stereotypical associations over anti-stereotypical ones in sentence-completion tasks, using the 'stereotype score (SS)'. An ideal, unbiased score is 50%.
findings: The proposed method of using synthetic data generated by ChatGPT effectively reduces religious bias. For GPT-2, the synthetic data outperformed baseline methods. For BERT, incorporating a 'loss-guided prompting' technique yielded the best results, surpassing baselines. Across other GPT-2 family models (LLaMA-3B, OPT-350m, GPT-Neo-125m), the 'general debiasing' strategy was highly effective, achieving an average bias reduction of 7.2%, while preserving the models' general language capabilities.
references: Julia Angwin, Jeff Larson, Surya Mattu, and Lauren Kirchner. Machine bias. In Ethics of data and analytics, pp. 254–264. Auerbach Publications, 2022.
